source:
What if I didn’t flower? What if my petals weren’t white? Cloud White. But dirty. Or black. Or none. 

I could be grass. Trampled. Eaten. Dug up. Tossed. No second thought. No thought at all, really. 

The humans who pass through. Destructive creatures. They give me thought. A small one. They gaze. I gaze back. They rip a flower from me. Place it by a stone slab. One moon cycle passes. My flower is back. 

I have a little beauty. A little protection. It is how I survive. This enclosure. How I thrive. Roots deeper than ever. 

I tell the grass – humans may dig you up. Bury more dead. “I’d be worried, if I were you.” 

Grass says he is not worried. “We’re dangerous. We’re made of blades.” 

Hehehe… 

That’s good. A good way to be.
target:
要是我不開花呢？要是花瓣不是白色呢？雲朵般的白。而是髒的，黑的，或者沒有。

我可能就是草。被踩，被吃，被挖起，丟掉。沒人多想。其實，根本不想。

那些路過的人類，破壞性的生物。他們會想到我，一點點。他們看我，我看回去。他們摘走我的一朵花，放在石板旁。一輪月過去，我的花又回來。

我有一點美麗，一點保護。所以能在這圍地裡活下去，繁盛生長。根比從前更深。

我對草說，人類可能把你挖掉，埋更多死人。「我是你的話，就會擔心。」

草說他不擔心。「我們很危險，每片葉子都是刀片。」

嘿嘿嘿……

很好。這樣活著，很好。

Thus, I graciously accept leading on horseback your exclusive contingent of light dragoons, the Black Cloaks as it were. Rest assured that I shall keep the fiercest demeanor in enforcing order within Bancroft and its surrounds, and I shall ensure safety of the Crown’s trade convoys therebetween. Our reputation shall be unforgiving.    

I confess, I do also thirst for vengeance. Robbed of my healthy gait by a lowly, savage-loving peasant, ‘tis my sincere pleasure to keep his likes heeled. 

Your loyal and humble servant,
Captain Oliver P. Ratliffe

Colonel Ainsworth, 

You have my deepest gratitude. I humbly affirm my duties to the Crown and most ardently accept the objectives presented in your previous missive. 

In truth, my injured leg, though earning me commendation to Captain from the Indian wars, has cloistered my fighting spirit to various offices and buried it beneath reams of correspondence and ledger work. Ever since the Americans rebelled in Boston years ago, I have longed for the day that allows my return to the field. I find that even a good woman is less invigorating than gunpowder smoke filling the lungs.

source:
What a summer. A full season of bragging. Flaunting. Razzing the grass. 

Late Spring. Newcomers. A colony of ground beetles. They enjoy my buds. Decide to stay and build. Ambitious. They begin an underhive. Eat pests, aphids and mites that bother us. Loosen the soil. I look to grass – do you enjoy this comfort I bring? 

Silence. So I ask again. And again. With each dewy morning. For a whole moon cycle. Hehehehe! 

Then the hottest days. Bees arrive. What lovely buzzing. A chorus of buzz. They sing. They dance on my flowers. Day in. Day out. I ask grass – do you enjoy the show I bring? 

Sweet, sweet silence. So I ask again. And again. With each dewy morning. For a whole moon cycle. 

One afternoon. Close to the time of falling leaves. A garter snake slides in. Snake snacks. Eats a beetle. Another. Munch. Munch. Swoop! A hawk! Amazing! Rips the snake from the grass and flies. We all gasp. First time we see this sky predator up close. I ask grass – will this make a good story?

Such perfect Silence. So I ask again. And again. With each morning chill. As winter sleep takes me. Nice and slow.  

And grass says, “Thanks to you, I appreciate winter now.”
target:
好一個夏天。整季吹噓，炫耀，逗弄那棵草。

暮春，新客人。一群步行蟲，喜歡我的花苞，決定留下建家。雄心勃勃，開始築地下巢。吃掉騷擾我們的害蟲、蚜蟲和蟎，鬆開土壤。我看向草：喜歡我帶來的舒適嗎？

沉默。所以我再問，再問。每個有露的早晨，問了整整一輪月。嘿嘿嘿！

接著，最熱的日子。蜜蜂來了，好可愛的嗡嗡聲，嗡嗡大合唱。牠們歌唱，在我的花上跳舞。一天又一天。我問草：喜歡我帶來的表演嗎？

甜美，甜美的沉默。所以我再問，再問。每個有露的早晨，問了整整一輪月。

一天下午，快到落葉時節。一條襪帶蛇滑進來，吃點心，吞一隻甲蟲，再一隻。嚼，嚼。唰！一隻鷹！驚人！從草間抓走蛇，飛了。我們全倒抽一口氣，第一次近看這種天空獵人。我問草：這能成為好故事嗎？

完美的沉默。所以我再問，再問。每個清冷的早晨，直到冬眠慢慢、舒舒服服地帶走我。

草說：「多虧你，我現在懂得欣賞冬天了。」

My duty in Asbury is to maintain order – a welcome change from the horrors of field combat. Among various other objectives, I am ordered to stifle Confederate
